headline: Researchers find flaws letting hackers remotely unlock and start connected cars
summary: Security researchers disclosed now-patched flaws in two automakers' systems that let them remotely unlock doors and start engines of net-connected vehicles in Australia and the US, chaining web application firewall bypasses and default logins.

claims.statement: Researchers found flaws letting them remotely unlock doors and start the engine of connected vehicles from two automakers.

sources.quote: Researchers pwn automakers’ Android apps to remotely unlock cars, honk horns
All net-connected vehicles from two major automakers allowed hackers to remotely unlock doors and start the engine
now-patched failures with API backend security showcase a lack of 101-level best practices

claims.statement: The researchers used WAF bypasses and default login credentials to command vehicles in Australia and the US.

sources.quote: Pair of researchers chain WAF bypasses and default logins to command vehicles in Australia and the US
